subject: Urgent: ClearWave reserved throughput shortfall and sustained 5xx spike
messages:
From: ops@clearwave.com (Maya Patel)
To: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Cc: cfo@clearwave.com
Date: Fri, 11 May 2028 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Spike in 5xx and tokens throttled against reserved pool — urgent

Jordan —

We started seeing a sustained 5xx surge at ~08:50 UTC this morning and a corresponding jump in tail latency. Our dashboard shows that the reserved capacity for our Dedicated pool is hitting the ceiling and requests are being routed to a lower-tier fallback model which is failing for ~18% of calls (5xx or timeouts). This is causing data-processing jobs to back up and a couple of downstream pipelines have already timed out during scheduled runs.

I attached a short error dump and a usage snapshot. Can Redwood confirm whether this is a dedicated pool saturation or a routing/config issue on ClearWave's end? We are on an enterprise reserved contract and this is impacting SLA obligations.

Maya Patel
Director, Engineering Ops
ClearWave Analytics
attachments: clearwave_error_log_20280511.txt, reserved_usage_snapshot_20280511.png
From: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
To: ops@clearwave.com (Maya Patel)
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 11 May 2028 09:28:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx and tokens throttled against reserved pool — urgent

Thanks for the quick flag, Maya. I'm escalating internally and we'll stand up a bridge. Preliminary ask: can you share the most recent span of request IDs (a 5–10 minute slice) so our SREs can correlate traces? We'll aim to determine whether this is: (A) true Dedicated pool saturation, (B) autoscaler misconfiguration, or (C) an anomalous traffic pattern from your side that triggers fallback behavior.

Marissa, David — looping you both for incident triage and customer communication. This is a high-priority reserved-capacity impact for ClearWave (Deal RW-CLR-2028-42).

Immediate next steps I propose:
- SRE (Sojin/David) to check Dedicated pool headroom and queueing metrics (KV cache backlog, queue depth, active batch sizes).
- Marissa to coordinate an ops bridge with ClearWave for a 09:45 UTC call and prepare a one-slide summary for execs.
- Customer: please paste 10 sample request IDs + timestamps in-thread.

I'll stay on the bridge.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: jordan_blake@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 11 May 2028 09:35:00 +0000
Subject: Internal: ClearWave dedicated pool triage & exec flag

Team —

Summary: ClearWave reports sustained 5xx and latency; appears tied to reserved pool capacity exhaustion and fallback to older model variants. Customer is in production and this is impacting batch jobs that run hourly. They are requesting immediate remediation and may escalate to CFO/CEO if unresolved by EOD.

Priority actions:
1) Soojin: can you confirm current headroom across the ClearWave dedicated pool (pool id rw-dedicated-16), active queue depth, and whether any other tenants recently spilled into the same host group? Provide metrics for the 08:30–09:30 UTC window.
2) David: check whether any recent routing policy changes or model variant promotions were applied to ClearWave's workspace in the last 72 hours.
3) Jordan: prep an audience-ready one-pager for execs outlining options (temporary burst, short-term credits, or immediate rollback to locked model version).

Exec escalation: recommend we pre-authorize a one-time emergency burst (up to 2x reserved for 3 hours) while engineering triages. I'll ping VP Sales and the CRO if we need a formal credit/commit authorization.

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 11 May 2028 09:43:12 +0000
Subject: Re: Internal: ClearWave dedicated pool triage & exec flag

On Fri, 11 May 2028 at 09:35, marissa_cole@redwood.ai wrote:
> Team —
>
> Summary: ClearWave reports sustained 5xx and latency; appears tied to reserved pool capacity exhaustion and fallback to older model variants.
>
Quick telemetry update:
- Pool rw-dedicated-16 shows CPU/GPU utilization sustained at 98% for the 08:45–09:15 UTC window, with token queue depth spiking to >1200 requests and tail latency > 2.8s.
- KV cache hit rate dropped by ~24% during the spike, increasing end-to-end token generation work.
- We observed spillover from a short-lived canary job (customer internal id: canary-9) that concurrently triggered large-batch inference jobs at 08:41 UTC. That likely pushed the pool past the autoscaler threshold.

Immediate mitigations applied (09:40 UTC):
- Activated emergency burst + routed excess to the dedicated burst pool (limited capacity) to reduce observed 5xx rate from 18% -> 6% over 10m.
- Temporarily increased preemption sensitivity to favor reserved tenants.

Next: we need approval for a 3-hour emergency burst (2x reserved) to stabilize ClearWave while we: (a) evict the canary workloads from that host group, (b) examine autoscaler hysteresis thresholds, and (c) provision a longer-term cap increase if needed.

Soojin Lee
Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
To: ops@clearwave.com (Maya Patel)
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai, cfo@clearwave.com (Liam O'Connor)
Date: Sat, 12 May 2028 17:48:00 +0000
Subject: ClearWave update and proposed customer remediation (credit + burst authorization)

Maya / Liam —

Thanks for your patience. Quick recap and plan after the internal triage:

What happened:
- A concurrent large-batch canary job from another tenant caused transient spillover into ClearWave's dedicated host group, saturating rw-dedicated-16 and driving fallback behavior that produced the 5xx/timeouts.
- SREs applied an emergency burst and preemption changes which brought 5xx down to ~6% within 10 minutes.

What we propose as remediation (short-term):
1) Immediate: pre-authorize a 3-hour emergency burst at 2x reserved capacity while we complete eviction of noisy tenants (already in progress). This is operationally low-risk and buys stability.
2) Compensation: Redwood proposes a one-time credit equal to 10% of this month's invoice for measurable SLA impact during the incident window. We also commit to a technical RCA and follow-up changes to autoscaler hysteresis within 72 hours.
3) Long-term: we recommend moving ClearWave to a slightly larger reserved tier (rw-reserve-L) or adding a dedicated isolation policy that prevents cross-tenant canary spillover. We'll prepare a cost/benefit and timeline for both options.

Please confirm acceptance of the emergency burst and the proposed credit so we can finalize the bridge notes and close the customer's escalated channel. If you'd prefer a call, we're ready to join a short exec bridge now.

Thanks — we're treating this as top priority.

Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
